claims.text: The as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is in an ordered single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited transition produces a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
The as-deposited alloy has substantial hysteresis during magnetic-field cycling.
Controlled annealing below the transition temperature can induce a moderate degree of short-range chemical disorder in the FeMnNiGeSi-type film.
The proposed annealing treatment can induce disorder without causing phase separation or compromising mechanical stability.
Annealing-induced short-range chemical disorder will be localized primarily at grain boundaries and interfacial regions.
Short-range chemical disorder at boundaries and interfaces modulates the nucleation barrier and kinetics of the magnetostructural transition.
Moderate chemical disorder disrupts nucleation and pinning sites associated with the first-order magnetostructural transition.
The introduced disorder reduces pinning of the moving magnetostructural interface.
Reduced interface pinning lowers the energy barrier for the phase transformation.
Annealed samples will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric entropy-change peak than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a moderately lower peak entropy-change magnitude than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit markedly reduced hysteresis under low-field cycling relative to the as-deposited baseline.
A thin-film geometry provides a high surface-to-volume ratio that enables rapid heat exchange.
The predictions apply to similarly deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films when low-temperature treatment induces disorder without secondary-phase formation.
Excessive disorder may change the predicted effects.
A substantial departure from thin-film geometry may change the predicted effects.
The magnitude of the entropy-change and hysteresis shifts depends on annealing parameters and resulting microstructural evolution.
